subject: Recap: Galileo reliability evaluation + fallthrough & test plan
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@galileohealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Galileo reliability evaluation + fallthrough & test plan

Hi Alex — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap of what we heard and a proposed next-steps/test plan so we stay aligned.

Call highlights
- Primary goals: predictable tail latency at scale, graceful degradation during infra incidents, and clear error-budget accounting for regulatory SLAs.
- Current evaluation: you’re running a mix of steady chat generation and bursty population-level inference (peaks ~120 QPS).
- Major competitors in scope: Hyperscaler managed endpoints (HyperscaleCloud), GenericAPI vendors, and an internal self-host attempt.

Redwood differentiators to validate in tests
- Smart routing + model fallthrough: automatic fallback to lower-cost compatible variants with consistent output quality constraints.
- Prefix/KV caching to lower per-token cost on conversation workloads while preserving latency SLOs.
- Built-in throttling and token-level cost visibility to avoid silent error-budget burn.
- Dedicated reserved pools available if you want hard capacity guarantees during go-live.

Proposed reliability test matrix (short list; full plan attached)
1) Sustained throughput soak: 2 hours at 90 QPS steady + 10% spikes; measure p50/p95/p99 latency and error rates.
2) Surge & cold-start: 0->200 QPS ramp in 3 minutes to test cold-start and burst tail latencies.
3) Failover simulation: simulate a region outage (route ~40% traffic to fallback region) and measure failover time and error budget hit.
4) Throttle handling: intentionally exceed per-route rate limit to observe graceful 429s vs silent drops and retry behavior.
5) Error-budget burn scenario: artificially inject node failures to cause 1% availability degradation and validate alerting and automatic fallback.

Owners & timing
- Redwood engineering lead: Ben Carter — will run the harness and share raw logs.
- Redwood product: Marissa Cole — will codify metrics and dashboard queries.
- Proposed dates: Aug 16–18 for initial runs (can compress to a single day if you prefer).

Next asks from your side
- Confirm stakeholder list (procurement/security) and whether the vendor security questionnaire needs completion before tests.
- Provide a sample workload (QPS profile + typical prompt sizes) or permission to replay recorded production traces.

I attached a compact test plan and a one-page summary of our fallthrough behavior. If this looks good I’ll schedule the harness run and loop in Ben for the logs.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Principal Solutions Engineer 
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Recap: Galileo reliability evaluation + fallthrough & test plan

Alex — good questions, answered inline below. Grace is looping in product security and will handle the questionnaire. Ben will own the harness and logs.

Q: fallback region KV cache behavior
A: By default, fallthrough creates a fresh instance in the fallback region (cold KV). We can also configure cross-region prefix replication for KV cache as a pre-provisioned option (adds ~2–3% token cost and requires a small provisioning window). We’ll run both variants in the plan: (a) cold-cache failover and (b) pre-replicated prefix mode so you can see the delta.

Q: questionnaire timing
A: Grace expects to complete the initial Q&A within 3 business days once she has the document (she grabbed the attachment). If there are SOC2 evidence asks we’ll surface them and coordinate with your security contact.

Attachments I’m sharing: 1) compact runbook with exact metrics we’ll publish (p50/p95/p99, availability windows, error-budget burn chart example), 2) a short executive summary template for the architecture committee.

Ben — can you confirm you can run both the cold-cache and prefix-replicated failover runs and share a sample of the raw p99 latency traces?

Thanks,
Jordan
